memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Your strength will be spent in vain, because your soil will not yield
its crops, nor will the trees of your land yield their fruit'"
- Lev 26:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the saddest phrases in Scripture: your strength will be
spent in vain. All the effort, all the striving, all the hard work — and
nothing to show for it. Not because they were lazy, but because they were
labouring apart from God's blessing.

There is a deep lesson here that reaches far beyond ancient Israel. Human
effort disconnected from God ultimately exhausts itself. We can pour out
enormous energy and still end up empty-handed.

Dear friend, have you known this feeling? The exhaustion of striving
without any sense of fruit? Working harder and harder, yet the soul grows
emptier? Sometimes God allows our self-powered efforts to come up dry
precisely so that we will stop and turn back to Him.

The psalmist wrote, unless the LORD builds the house, the builders labour
in vain (Ps 127:1). Notice — the builders still labour. There is real
effort. But without the Lord, it comes to nothing.

This is actually a mercy. If our striving apart from God always
succeeded, we would never learn to depend on Him. The very emptiness of
self-willed effort is God's kindness, turning us home.

Jesus offers a different way: come to me, all you who are weary and
burdened, and I will give you rest (Matt 11:28). The answer to fruitless
striving is not to try harder but to return to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I exhausting myself striving apart from God's help?
2. What am I building that God has not been part of?
3. How might my present weariness be an invitation to return to Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I am tired of striving in my own strength. Teach me to labour
with You rather than apart from You, and give my weary soul the rest that
only Christ provides. Amen.
